body: Forward test of the promise-tracker credibility method (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Probability 0.45 (naive base rate 0.60) that: Navin Fluorine confirms the Chemours (advanced-cooling) project was commissioned by 31-Dec-2026. Evidence: Q2 FY27 call (30-Oct-2026): 'The Chemours project… is also progressing towards commissioning in Q3 FY27.' Analyst notes 'we've seen some delay'; MD Anish Ganatra calls the delay 'a conscious choice' over process route. Other promises in the same call: R32/HFC expansion 'on track for commissioning shortly'; cGMP-4 Phase 2 (~₹125 cr) operational by end Q4 FY27; MPP debottleneck commissioned Sep-2026 (a kept promise). Reasoning: Promise-tracker prior: a project that has already slipped once has a materially higher chance of slipping again, even when the remaining window is short; partner-dependent qualification adds risk. Navin's other recent near-term promises were kept, which keeps us from going lower. Resolution: YES if a Navin filing, press release, investor presentation or the Q3 FY27 earnings call states that the Chemours/advanced-cooling (two-phase immersion fluid) plant was commissioned (mechanically complete and started production) on or before 31-Dec-2026. 'Commissioning in Q4'/'in January' = NO. Source: Navin Fluorine Q3 FY27 results presentation / earnings call transcript / NSE announcements. Resolve by 2027-02-28; score with Brier vs base rate.
